gaps.sentence: Every one of the switches ___ been tested twice.
gaps.explanation: 'Every one of' takes a singular verb: has.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the workforce is part-time now.
gaps.hint: pattern: ___ of + specific group; singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Half of the workforce is ...' is the correct pattern; 'the half of' is not used in this position.

gaps.sentence: Hardly ___ of the villagers had ever seen a passport.
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly any of' = almost none of; 'hardly none' is impossible.
'Too cold to swim' means the temperature prevents swimming; 'enough' would follow the adjective.

gaps.sentence: It's so quiet here — there's hardly ___ around.
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly' is a negative adverb, so it combines with 'anybody' (hardly anybody = almost nobody); 'nobody' would double the negative.

gaps.hint: general statement without 'the' — 'people' has no article
gaps.explanation: 'Most people' means people in general; 'most of' needs 'the' (most of the people).

gaps.sentence: I looked everywhere, but I couldn't find my keys ___.
gaps.explanation: After a negative verb, 'anywhere' is used; 'somewhere' belongs to affirmative sentences.

gaps.sentence: ___ smells burnt in here — can you check the oven?
gaps.hint: affirmative statement about an unknown thing
gaps.explanation: 'Something' is used in affirmative sentences for an unknown thing; the request to check the oven shows the speaker believes it.
